title: Incident lifecycle orchestration and notification templates
author: Elena Park
content:
Summary

This document defines the standardized incident lifecycle orchestration used by Redwood Inference SRE and Platform teams. It contains:
- a concise incident classification matrix and SLO thresholds,
- an ordered runbook for common service classes (serving runtime, model routing, cache failures, and networking),
- an escalation matrix with clear ownership,
- on-call rotation and game day playbook templates, and
- copy-ready status page and customer communication templates for each incident phase.

Scope

Applies to all production services that provide inference capabilities (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control plane). Does not replace service-specific runbooks; instead this is the orchestration and communications layer that ties those runbooks together.

Owners and roles

- Incident Commander (IC): typically the first senior on-call for the owning service team. Responsible for overall triage and customer communications.
- Primary Responder: on-call engineer assigned to the affected service. Leads technical mitigation steps.
- Platform SRE: supports systemic failures (networking, infra, capacity).
- Communications Lead: product or support engineer who owns status page & customer messages.
- Postmortem Author: assigned after recovery; owns a blameless postmortem and follow-up tasks.

Severity classification (quick reference)

| Severity | Symptom examples | Availability impact | Typical initial action | Pager? | Escalation lead |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Sev0 (Critical) | Global outage (hosting API down), control plane unreachable, major data loss | Total or near-total outage for >50% customers | Pager and immediate conference bridge | yes | IC + Eng Director |
| Sev1 (High) | Large regional outage, major API latency regression causing timeouts | Significant degradation affecting many customers | Pager, rapid mitigation, traffic steering | yes | IC + Platform SRE |
| Sev2 (Medium) | Single-region degraded performance, increased error rates for a subset of routes | Partial customer impact, workarounds available | Channel alert (Slack) | maybe | Primary Responder |
| Sev3 (Low) | Minor errors, performance under SLO in non-critical path | Informational | Ticket and monitor | no | Service owner |

SLOs and thresholds

- Platform availability SLO (global): 99.95% monthly for request success (2xx/3xx) across hosted API.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency < 350ms for short requests (<=128 tokens).
- Error budget policy: weekly burn above 2% of monthly error budget triggers immediate review and possible canary rollback.

Immediate containment checklist (first 10 minutes)

1. Acknowledge pager in on-call channel and start an incident thread.
2. IC creates an incident channel (#incident-<short-name>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>).
3. Triage: confirm scope (global/region/customer), affected models/routes, recent deploys, and capacity events.
4. Apply short-lived mitigation: scale up reserved capacity, enable fallback model variant, or toggle rate-limiter to shed non-critical traffic.
5. Post initial status to status.redwood.ai (see templates below).
6. If Sev0/Sev1, stand up a conference bridge and invite Platform SRE, Primary Responder, and Communications Lead.

Detailed runbooks (select service classes)

A. High latency / tail-latency spike (serving runtime)

1. Identify affected endpoints: `curl -s https://metrics.redwood.ai/query?service=serving&window=5m` (internal metrics endpoint).
2. Confirm p95 and p99 from Grafana dashboards: `Dashboard: Runtime > latencies > p95/p99` (link).
3. Check recent kernel/driver updates on GPU fleet: `fleetctl recent-updates --since 1h`
4. Inspect runtime logs for KV cache thrashing or OOMs: `kubectl -n serving logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --tail 200`
5. Mitigations (ordered):
   - Temporarily reduce batch size for the affected model in the route config: `redwoodctl route update --route <route> --batch-size <smaller>`
   - Enable model fallback to smaller quantized variant: `redwoodctl model override --route <route> --model <variant>`
   - Add ephemeral nodes to the pool (if autoscale lagging): `k8s-autoscaler scale --pool serving-pool --delta +4`
6. Confirm impact reduction and update status message. If unchanged after 15 minutes, escalate to Platform SRE for kernel-level investigation.

B. Cache/KV eviction causing regeneration storms

1. Check cache hit ratio: `redis-cli info stats` or dashboard.
2. If hit ratio < 10% and requests spike, enable prefix caching for hot prefixes: `redwoodctl cache configure --route <route> --prefix-caching true`
3. Increase KV-TTL as a temporary measure and add circuit-breaker to limit cold-start concurrency: `redwoodctl cache set-ttl --route <route> --ttl 600`
4. If root cause is capacity, spin up additional cache replicas and route small percentage of traffic to standby cache.

C. Model-serving OOMs or kernel crashes

1. Identify crashing pod: `kubectl -n serving get pods --selector=model=<model-name>`
2. Describe crash: `kubectl -n serving describe pod <pod>` and `kubectl -n serving logs <pod> --previous`
3. If reproducible on a specific model variant, remove that variant from rotation and redirect to a known-good variant.
4. Collect core dump and upload to /artifacts/incidents/<id>/ for research.

Escalation matrix and contact rules

- Primary Responder (first 10 min): attempt containment and basic mitigation.
- If issue persists 15 minutes (Sev1) escalate to Platform SRE.
- If lack of progress after 30 minutes or service impact widens (Sev0), involve Eng Director and Product TPM.
- For customer-impacting incidents (any customer SLA at risk) notify Customer Success within 20 minutes.

Escalation contact table:

| Role | Pager | Slack handle | Backup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary Responder | pager:svc-team | @svc-oncall | @svc-senior |
| Platform SRE | pager:sre | @platform-sre | @sre-lead |
| Eng Director | pager:dir | @eng-dir | @vp-eng |
| Customer Success | pager:cs | @customer-success | @cs-lead |

On-call rotation & handoff checklist

- Rotation cadence: 1 week for service primary on-call.
- Handoff process (10 min): outgoing must post a Handoff Note in #oncall-handoffs with:
  - current incidents and their status,
  - ongoing mitigations and TODOs,
  - saddest alarms and any scheduled changes in the next 24 hours.
- Shadowing: new oncallers shadow for first 48 hours with a senior oncall.
- On-call health: limit to 3 on-call weeks / quarter per engineer; opt-out and replacements handled by team lead.

Game day plan (quarterly)

Objective: validate orchestration and communications in a low-risk environment. Each game day tests a different failure mode (large-scale latency spike, cross-region partition, model rollback).

Standard game day flow:
1. Pre-game checklist (1 week out): pick scenario, notify participating teams, create test incident channel, and provision test tenants.
2. Execution (hour): trigger scenario via the agreed simulated fault injection harness (link to harness).
3. Observability: runbook author monitors dashboards and ensures metrics are captured.
4. Communications: practice status page updates and CS messaging.
5. Post-game: 48-hour retrospective with action items assigned.

Status page & customer communication templates

- Best practices for customer messages: be timely (within 20 minutes for major outages), factual, and set expectations for the next update. Use clear placeholders for impacted regions, estimated time to fix (ETTF), and mitigation steps.

Template: Initial status (post within 20 minutes)

Title: "[Incident] Service disruption affecting inference API — investigation underway"
Status: Investigating
Impact: Some customers in <region(s)> may experience elevated latency and errors when calling /v1/generate.
Scope: A subset of model routes; not all customers.
What we are doing: Our engineers have identified increased tail latency in the serving runtime and are performing mitigations including traffic steering and model fallbacks.
Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner as new information becomes available.
Contact: support@redwood.ai (link to status page).

Template: Follow-up update

Title: "[Update] Mitigations applied; partial recovery for affected routes"
Status: Partial Service Restored
Summary: We enabled model fallbacks and scaled serving pools; error rates decreased by ~70% for impacted routes.
Remaining impact: A small percentage of requests may still see elevated latency.
ETTF: Further improvements expected within 1 hour; we continue monitoring.

Template: Resolution

Title: "[Resolved] Inference API incident — full service restored"
Status: Resolved
Summary: Root cause was a kernel-level regression in our GPU runtime affecting batch scheduling. A rollback to the previous runtime release removed the regression.
Customer impact: Customers may have observed increased error rates and latency between HH:MM and HH:MM UTC. No data loss was observed.
Next steps: A post-incident review is scheduled and we will publish a summary with action items.

Template: Postmortem summary (public-friendly)

Title: "Postmortem: Inference API latency incident on <date>"
Impact: Brief summary of affected customers and metrics (e.g. p95 increased from 120ms -> 1800ms for X minutes).
Timeline: numbered timeline with timestamps for detection, escalation, mitigation, and resolution.
Root cause: concise statement.
Corrective actions: list with owners and ETA.

Internal postmortem checklist

1. IC assigns postmortem owner within 24 hours.
2. Collect logs, traces, and metrics into /artifacts/incidents/<id>/.
3. Create a blameless timeline and review with stakeholders within 72 hours.
4. Track corrective actions in backlog; require at least one action to be assigned to fix the root cause before closing the incident.

Tools & useful commands (quick reference)

- redwoodctl status routes --service <service> --json  # returns route health
- cockpit logs --service serving --since 10m  # aggregated recent logs
- fleetctl capacity list --pool serving-pool  # capacity view
- grafana: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/serving/runtime

Post-incident review and metrics to track

- Time to detect, time to engage, time to mitigate, time to resolve.
- SLO burn during incident, error budget remaining.
- Number of customers affected and estimated outage minutes.
- Follow-up action completion rate.

Appendix: Example status page JSON payload (internal)

{
  "incident_id": "INC-<id>",
  "status": "investigating",
  "impact_summary": "Elevated latency for generation API in us-west1",
  "first_reported_at": "<ISO timestamp>",
  "next_update_in_minutes": "30"
}

(Use the status page CLI: `statusctl create --payload file://status.json`)

Final notes

This orchestration guide is intentionally prescriptive for the first 30 minutes of an incident to reduce cognitive load for responders. Service-specific runbooks should be referenced for technical details. Regularly run the game day playbook and keep the communications templates updated; Communications Lead should validate customer-facing copy quarterly.

-- End of document --
